Yesterday's log is small: it has only 5 requests and no timestamps.

| Status | Count | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 2xx (200, 201) | 2 | 40% |
| 4xx (404) | 1 | 20% |
| 5xx (500, 502) | 2 | 40% |

- **Server errors:** 40% of requests failed on the server side. Both failures were `GET /b`, which returned a 500 and then a 502. Every request to `/b` failed, so that endpoint looks broken. The 502 suggests an upstream or gateway problem, and the 500 suggests an application error.
- **Client error:** The 404 was on `GET /a`, which also returned a 200 once. It's probably a missing resource or a bad link, and it looks minor.
- **Working paths:** `GET /a` returned a 200, and `POST /c` returned a 201.

If `/b` is a page users hit often, that fits "the site felt broken". But five lines can't show how widespread it was. The log has no timestamps, so I can't say when it started, how long it lasted, or whether it was a burst or ongoing. It also doesn't show how many users were affected, and it may be a truncated sample.

`app.log` in the same directory might show what caused the 500 and 502 on `/b`. I haven't opened it. I can check it next, or look at a fuller log export if you have one.
